clue.text: Winger making ill-natured charge

parts.note: someone ill-natured is cross, bad-tempered
a bill is a charge for goods or services

explanation.surface: Someone is levying a spiteful, unfair fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the flank, but here it is simply a creature with wings: a finch with crossed mandibles.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch, a bird, and birds are creatures that fly on wings.

clue.text: Outstanding sculpture adjudicator having lie-in

indicators.note: having here means holding, so the referee holds the lie inside it

parts.note: ref, referee, is an adjudicator
the lie of lie-in is the word put in

explanation.surface: A judge's lie-in is a remarkable carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lie-in' is read as having LIE in: REF holds LIE. 'Outstanding' means standing out, as carving in relief does.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is a carving in which figures project from a flat background, standing out from it.

clue.text: Bent French painter turning up about midnight

indicators.note: the painter's name, turned, goes about, around, the midnight letter
in a down clue turning up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter
G is the middle letter of night

explanation.surface: A stooping French artist overturns things around twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses DEGAS to SAGED; 'about' puts it round G, the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has sagged sinks or bends downwards under weight.

clue.text: Give away punt and beam

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a wager
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone donates a boat and a timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' looks like the boat and 'beam' like timber; they are a wager and a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a secret or person is to reveal or hand them over disloyally.

clue.text: Many an aquatic bird is light

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, used for many
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Plenty of water birds are not heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a lamp in a protective case, a portable source of illumination.

clue.text: Popular officer as a rule

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked commander is usually the case.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually, for the most part.

clue.text: Cut and then join together one by one

parts.note: to sever is to cut
to ally is to unite, join together

explanation.surface: Split up and then reunite, each in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally means separately, each individually.

clue.text: Leading, so maybe standing by

explanation.surface: Someone at the front is perhaps waiting in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading a horse or a companion you walk at its side, so beside it; 'standing by' is a plain sense of beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means close beside, next to, which is where you walk when guiding a horse and where a supporter stands.

clue.text: A continental way to dance and unwind

parts.note: un is the French for 'a', so a continental 'a'
a reel is a lively Scottish country dance

explanation.surface: A European's method of dancing helps them relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A continental' means 'a' in a continental language: French UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unreel is to unwind a line or film from a spool.

clue.text: Paving the colour of the irises

indicators.note: the colour of the irises is their colour, so the iris word comes first and the colour word follows

parts.note: a flag is the common name for the wild yellow iris, so irises are flags
tone means a shade or colour

explanation.surface: Someone describes a paint shade as matching the irises of eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irises' reads as part of the eye, but a flag is a wild iris plant, so the clue means the flag's tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are flat slabs laid as paving for paths and floors.

clue.text: Within this his eminence has to hold back

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Eminence, a cardinal's title
to rein in is to hold back, restrain

explanation.surface: A cardinal must restrain himself within these walls.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Eminence (also His Excellency); 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Herein is a formal word meaning in this document or place.

clue.text: Great need might be brought about

indicators.note: the letters of the two words might be rearranged into something else, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pressing necessity could be created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' signals that GREAT NEED can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to produce or cause it, so generated is caused or produced.

clue.text: Bearing with friends — some bloomer!

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
pals are friends

explanation.surface: Someone carrying themselves among mates makes a real gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flowering plant: sepals are part of one, so 'some' bloomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepals are the leaf-like outer parts of a flower, a portion of any plant that blooms.

clue.text: Involve the troublesome child with a story about a furry animal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: the story word goes about, around, the animal

parts.note: a lie is a false story
a cat is a furry animal

explanation.surface: Drag in the naughty kid along with a tale about a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining IMP to LI(CAT)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be concerned in a crime, entangling them.

clue.text: Lay down rules for page concerning writer

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Set regulations for a boy servant about an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a young attendant but is P; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To prescribe is to state authoritatively what must be done.

clue.text: Sea shanty "the dividing line"

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a shanty is a crude hut, a shed

explanation.surface: A sailors' song is said to be the dividing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea shanty' reads as a sailors' song, but shanty is a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is the ridge separating river basins, hence a turning point or dividing line.

clue.text: A tip is the aim

explanation.surface: Advice about the goal of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an extremity or point, and also a purpose or goal one works towards.

clue.text: A fish has little feeling

indicators.note: the word has a little of itself, a small part, which is taken out

explanation.surface: A fish hardly feels anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has little' takes a small part of 'feeling'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a snake-like fish.

clue.text: Minister receiving a father

indicators.note: the minister's letters receive, take in, the a

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a minister's qualification

explanation.surface: A clergyman welcomes a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a degree for clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad is an informal word for a male parent.

clue.text: Football crowd staying behind to vandalise a seaside town

indicators.note: the crowd word stays behind the damage word, so it comes second

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
the gate is the number attending a match

explanation.surface: Fans linger after the game to wreck a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gate' is the attendance at a football match. MARGATE is a seaside resort in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a Kent resort on England's coast, a town by the sea.

clue.text: Helped a number and suffered for it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
ailed means was unwell, suffered

explanation.surface: Someone assisted a figure and paid the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for it' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, so availed means was of service.

clue.text: Given guidance and money — a couple of notes

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British unit of money
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone received advice, cash and a pair of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests banknotes beside 'money', but they are musical notes, letters from A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Led is the past participle of lead, to guide, so given guidance means directed.

clue.text: Noise or chaos can be wearing

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the words noise and or are jumbled

explanation.surface: Din or confusion can be exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like 'tiring', but it is the noun: gradual wearing away; 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil.

clue.text: Pay heed when a good man's in the right

indicators.note: the saint is put in, inside, the word for a legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Pay attention when a virtuous person is proved correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The right' suggests correctness, but a LIEN is a legal right over another's property; 'when' and the possessive 's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to attend to what is said, taking notice.

clue.text: Ineffectual woman — a sheepish creature

parts.note: wet is British slang for feeble, ineffectual
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A feeble woman is shy and timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' looks like 'shy', but a wether is a castrated ram, literally a sheep creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A wether is a castrated ram, a male sheep.

clue.text: Standard twinkling star's measurement

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a twinkling is a moment, a sec

explanation.surface: Normal flickering of a star is gauged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twinkling' looks like a star shining but means an instant: SEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is a unit of distance used in astronomy, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: Once fine port kept in the wrong environs

indicators.note: the port is kept in, held inside, the jumbled word
environs means surroundings, so the jumbled word surrounds the port
wrong means the word the is made wrong, its letters disordered

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: In the past a good harbour was held in the wrong surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the three letters into HET. 'Fine' is a penalty, not 'good', and 'Once' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A heriot was a feudal payment due to a lord on a tenant's death, a historical levy.

clue.text: Bears damage trees a lot

indicators.note: the words trees and a lot are damaged, broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Bears do a great deal of harm to woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, but it is the verb: puts up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, endure it.

clue.text: Show affection with caution on ocean-going craft

parts.note: care means caution
SS, steamship, is a ship that sails the ocean

explanation.surface: Be loving, but carefully, aboard a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle stroke, a tender touch expressing love.

clue.text: Flambés a joint and at sea that could spell danger

definitions.text: at sea that could spell danger

parts.note: to flambé food is to set it alight, so flambés means lights
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A chef sets fire to a cut of meat, and on a boat that is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a moored ship with a beacon marks a hazard at sea, so it spells danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is an anchored vessel with a beacon warning of shoals or rocks.

clue.text: Expert to be included in abstemious panel

indicators.note: the expert word is included in, put inside, the abstemious word

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from drink
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: A specialist joins a sober committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panel' suggests a committee, but it is a flat slab; TT is teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat slab bearing an inscription, a panel of stone or wood.

clue.text: Making up can tire — it is so complicated

indicators.note: making up means composing or putting together, so these words are recombined

explanation.surface: Applying cosmetics can be tiring because it is so fiddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' rearranges CAN TIRE IT; 'is so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate has many detailed, interwoven parts, hence complex.
